clue.text: Sharp bed of nails

definitions.meaning: sharp in the sense of fast, nimble or mentally alert
the sensitive flesh under the fingernails, the place nails sit on

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is fast or alert; the other is the tender flesh beneath a nail, as in 'bitten to the quick'.

clue.text: In other words, day covered by *Low'

definitions.text: In other words, day covered by *Low'

parts.note: quasi is Latin for as it were, so to speak

indicators.note: the day's letter sits inside the cow's call, which surrounds it

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Another name for the Sunday known as Low.
explanation.walkthrough: Quasimodo Sunday is the other name of Low Sunday, the Sunday after Easter, from its Latin introit 'Quasi modo geniti'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Sunday after Easter, Low Sunday, is also called by this Latin title.

clue.text: Eskimo has just one night in Paris

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
nuit is French for night

explanation.surface: A traveller from the Arctic spends a single night in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the Arctic people of Canada and Greenland once called Eskimos.

clue.text: Out east, whisk cakes as ingredients for trifles

indicators.note: the letters are mixed together like a recipe's components
the letter for east is taken out of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe telling you to beat sponge into a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out east' removes E from CAKES; 'as ingredients' mixes WHISK CAKS. 'trifles' looks like the dessert, but here means small trinkets.
explanation.definitionFit: Kickshaws are trinkets or fancy dainties, things of little value.

clue.text: According to the rules, say, do this before seeing the film

definitions.text: say, do this before seeing the film
definitions.meaning: reading the novel first, before watching its screen adaptation

explanation.surface: Advice that a stickler reads the novel before going to the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things strictly by regulation is an idiom; literally, it is reading the novel a movie came from.

clue.text: Directors receive fifty pounds in the post

indicators.note: the board takes in the two letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a board is a company's directors
L is the Roman numeral fifty
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Company directors are sent fifty quid by mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like the mail but is the definition: a short thick pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bollard is a short stout pillar, on a quayside or keeping traffic off a road.

clue.text: Completed, in spite of being interrupted by rain at first

indicators.note: a letter breaks into the word, interrupting it

parts.note: though means in spite of the fact that

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A match finished despite showers stopping play.
explanation.definitionFit: Through can mean finished, as in 'I'm through with this'.

clue.text: Draw out Egyptian leader

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Egyptian
duce is Italian for leader, Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Extracting information from a Cairo ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to elicit or bring out something latent, like a fact.

clue.text: People coming in continuously improving

indicators.note: the people enter the phrase, going inside it

parts.note: the two-word phrase 'on end' means without a break; this is its first word
the second word of 'on end', meaning without a break, as in for hours at a stretch
them means people in general, as in us and them

explanation.surface: Visitors keep arriving at a recovering patient's bedside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering from illness is getting better, an idiom for healing.

clue.text: Showed respect by kowtowing Nipponese emperors liked their heads being prominent

indicators.note: the heads of the words, their first letters, stand out and are taken

explanation.surface: Japanese emperors liked to see bowing subjects with heads visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' are the first letters of kowtowing, Nipponese, emperors, liked, their.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on one knee is a traditional gesture of deference.

clue.text: Kindly have lunch — dull fare, taken out of wrappings'

indicators.note: each word loses its outside letters, as if unwrapped, leaving only its inner part

explanation.surface: A complaint about a dreary packed lunch eaten from its paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out of wrappings' strips the first and last letters of each of have, lunch, dull, fare, leaving AV, UNC, UL, AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Avuncular means like a kindly uncle: genial, benevolent and friendly.

clue.text: Abroad one gets duty-free

parts.note: un is French for one, so one said abroad
a tie is an obligation or duty that binds you

explanation.surface: A traveller picks up duty-free goods on a trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty-free' looks like one phrase; split it so 'duty' gives TIE and 'free' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something knotted or bound is to loosen it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stress is cut with new treatment

indicators.note: the letters are given a new handling, rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A patient's tension eased by a fresh surgical cut.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ictus is the rhythmic accent or beat on a syllable in verse.

clue.text: Diversion intended to follow a residential street, it's said

indicators.note: the spoken phrase is heard as a single word of a different spelling

parts.words: intended to follow a residential street
parts.note: MEANT (intended) follows A MEWS, a mews being a residential street of converted stables

explanation.surface: Someone planned to walk down a quiet street for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' tells you to say A MEWS MEANT out loud. A mews is a British street of old stables turned into houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is entertainment or recreation, something that pleasantly passes the time.

clue.text: Casual worker away from work first

indicators.note: this word places the piece for being away from work at the front

parts.note: someone off is not at work today
a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A temp who comes in last after a day off.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual or careless, without much thought or courtesy.

clue.text: Engineers carried by plane or ship

indicators.note: the engineers ride inside the aircraft word

parts.note: a fighter is a military plane
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Military engineers transported by aircraft or boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ship' looks like a verb alongside 'carried', but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo vessel.

clue.text: One no longer important possesses money, according to auditor

parts.note: possesses means has

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: bean is old slang for a coin, as in 'not a bean'

explanation.surface: A faded celebrity whose wealth is checked by an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but means a hearer: BEAN said out loud sounds like BEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person whose fame or influence has faded away.

clue.text: Yesman will not accept damaged copy

indicators.note: the refusal word takes in the jumbled letters

parts.note: shan't is a contraction meaning shall not, will not

indicators.note: the word is spoiled, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A flatterer refuses a smudged photocopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will not' is the contraction SHANT; 'accept' looks like agreeing, but here the refusal word takes the jumbled letters into itself, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant is a flatterer who agrees with superiors to win favour.

clue.text: Calf in a state?

parts.note: a young animal of a Channel Island dairy breed, read as the name of an American state

explanation.definitionFit: This US state's name could describe a newborn of a Channel Islands dairy breed.

clue.text: Disregard poetry written in Old English

indicators.note: the poetry is placed inside the abbreviation for the old language

parts.note: verse means poetry

explanation.surface: A scholar dismisses ancient Anglo-Saxon poems.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic sense of oversee is to overlook, that is to fail to notice or ignore.

clue.text: English modest about record in bionomics

indicators.note: the shy word goes round the record

parts.note: coy means shy or modest
a log is a written record, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: A humble English scientist with a notebook studying living things.
explanation.definitionFit: Bionomics is an older name for the study of organisms and their environment.

clue.text: Family's abandoned thief, a pilferer from Rheims

annotationWithheld.why: Family's abandoned thief, a pilferer from Rheims (7): 'a pilferer from Rheims' defines it (the Jackdaw of Rheims), but no parse of 'Family's abandoned thief' gives the answer's letters, and a search found none.
annotationWithheld.clue: Family's abandoned thief, a pilferer from Rheims

clue.text: Nothing but diamonds? That's right

parts.note: just means only, nothing but
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player holding only diamonds is told that's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' suggests the card suit; it is ICE, slang for gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice means fairness, what is morally fair and due.

clue.text: Country merciful after deposing king gifted with discernment

indicators.note: the trimmed word comes after the country's letters

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa

indicators.note: the king is removed from the word, as a monarch is thrown off a throne

parts.note: gracious means merciful
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A revolution in a kindly nation that overthrows its monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacious means wise and shrewd, having keen judgement.

clue.text: Water's rising in the boat

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: pools are bodies of water

explanation.surface: Water is coming up inside a leaky vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Short bridge

definitions.meaning: to span or go over, as a bridge does

explanation.definitionFit: Being irritable is one sense; to go over or span a river is the other.

clue.text: Dough went slowly, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word is chosen for how it is heard, not how it is spelt

parts.note: paced means walked at a measured speed

explanation.surface: Bread rising sluggishly, judging from the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a soft mixture of flour and water, the same thing as a dough.

clue.text: Go off with money buried in the ground

indicators.note: the money goes inside the earth word, as if buried

parts.note: soil is the ground
P is the abbreviation for penny or pence

explanation.surface: Treasure hidden underground going to waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that goes off has gone bad, the same as rotting.

clue.text: Top alfresco party

parts.note: alfresco means in the open air, outside
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: The best outdoor party ever held.
explanation.definitionFit: To top something is to beat or surpass it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A proviso is set out, limiting you, say, to producing eggs

indicators.note: the scrambled letters close around the letter, hemming it in
the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

parts.note: U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A contract condition restricting you, oddly, to laying eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is set out' rearranges A PROVISO into OVIPAROS, and 'limiting' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviparous animals lay eggs that hatch outside the body, like birds.

clue.text: Though nameless, presently .I shall be represented in several columns

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new order
N, the abbreviation for name, is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: An anonymous writer promises a soon-to-come appearance in several newspaper columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N from PRESENTLY, giving PRESETLY; with I, 'shall be represented' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A peristyle is a colonnade, a row of pillars surrounding a courtyard or building.

clue.text: Keep the score in match

definitions.meaning: to count up points as a game goes on

explanation.definitionFit: A tally is a running count of points; two accounts that agree are said to tally.
